decisions.reason: A same-message MODIFY already records that the second V is a locked asset that must remain unchanged unless the client explicitly requests a change.
A same-message MODIFY already requires complete-wordmark exploration to preserve the locked Hero V, second V, and É accent unchanged.
A same-message MODIFY already records the É accent as a locked asset that must remain unchanged unless the client explicitly requests a change.
A same-message MODIFY already confines letterform exploration to work around the three locked assets while carrying them forward unchanged.

The candidate still describes one unified terminal gesture across both Vs and the É accent, while message 158 had excluded the expressive right-arm signature from the second V. Message 160 locks the three assets but does not clarify whether this older shared-terminal Requirement remains valid or should be narrowed.
Locking the three wordmark assets does not change the current brand-expression goals or visual-tone constraints.
The asset-lock decision does not change the deferred champagne-gold material treatment, its qualities, or its application sequence.
The decision to lock the Hero V, second V, and É accent does not alter the requirement for a wordmark-led identity without a separate icon or monogram.
